content.text: I’ll inspect the discussion, then trace the reported behavior into the current code and relevant tests. I’ll keep this diagnostic-only unless you ask me to implement a fix.

The report is well isolated: the native executable accepts stdin, while the PowerShell activation function fails during parameter binding. I’m checking the generated function and PowerShell’s pipeline semantics now, including whether a pass-through fix preserves argument handling and exit codes.

I reproduced it from the current checkout on PowerShell 7.6.5: the activated `mise` function emits the binding error and the wrapped command does not receive stdin; invoking the same binary path directly prints `data` and exits 0. The regression originates in the advanced-function parameter block added for Windows PowerShell 5 compatibility, so the reporter’s diagnosis is correct.

The report is valid and reproducible. No repository changes made.

- Root cause: the activated PowerShell wrapper is an advanced function whose only parameter uses `ValueFromRemainingArguments`; it has no `ValueFromPipeline` parameter. PowerShell rejects pipeline objects before `mise.exe` can receive stdin. See [src/shell/pwsh.rs](/Users/jdx/src/mise/src/shell/pwsh.rs:36).
- Confirmed locally with PowerShell 7.6.5:
  - Activated wrapper: binding error; wrapped command receives no input.
  - Direct `mise` binary: prints `data`, exits 0.
- This is not a task runner or CMake bug. Native `mise` already forwards stdin correctly.
- The regression was introduced by commit `7a7f4f3f55d70d7299701b65a9b42b5456084711` in [PR #6168](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/6168), when the advanced parameter block was added for Windows PowerShell 5 compatibility.
- Current PowerShell tests cover activation hooks but not stdin forwarding; [e2e-win/mise_hook.Tests.ps1](/Users/jdx/src/mise/e2e-win/mise_hook.Tests.ps1:1) is a reasonable home for a regression test.

Recommended fix: retain the PowerShell 5-compatible argument handling, add a non-positional `ValueFromPipeline` parameter, and forward `$input` into every native `mise` invocation. A simple implementation will buffer the PowerShell pipeline; a steppable-pipeline implementation would preserve streaming for large inputs. Either approach should be tested on both Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.

One adjacent finding: the wrapper also consumes PowerShell’s `--` end-of-parameters token, so commands such as `mise x -- command` fail through the function even without piping. That is separate from discussion [#12922](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/12922).
